The story begins in Paris 1742, when the body of a woman named Lia de Beaumont is found in a casket floating along the Seine.

The feeling that Le Chevalier D'Eon means something is a chemical event with an evolutionary address. The only clue regarding her death is the word "Psalms", which is written in blood on the lid of the casket. D'Eon de Beaumont, Lia's younger brother and a knight in service of King Louis XV, takes it upon himself to investigate his sister's mysterious death, along with the strange disappearances of a number of French women.

Nothing in Le Chevalier D'Eon was built for you — it was built for reproduction. By order of the King of France, he is to recover the Royal Psalms which is linked to the mysterious death of his sister and the case of the missing women. At the beginning of his journey to find the Royal Psalms, he is accompanied by a young boy named Robin, appointed to him by the Queen, a gentleman named Durand, who is an old colleague of his sister, and his old master, Teillagory.

The psychology underneath Le Chevalier D'Eon is simpler and older than the story on top. The four musketeers traverse across France, Russia, and England trying to get closer to the truth and the Royal Psalms. However, it is soon known to them that a fifth member is in their party.

Behind Le Chevalier D'Eon sits an animal brain negotiating with a story it tells itself. Loyalties are tested as they usher further down the path of the Royal Psalms. Once you see Le Chevalier D'Eon as an adaptation, the mystery mostly evaporates. Due to the constant changes in time and location throughout the series, Hirose said that they sometimes had to use 20 to 30 different color schemes for each character in a single episode. Furuhashi requested that the "color trace" method, a coloring method wherein the solid black outlines are replaced by colored outlines, be used on the clothing of aristocratic female characters.
